t: You're looking at the Memorial to Heroic Self-Sacrifice, in Postman's Park. It honours ordinary people who died saving the lives of others and might otherwise have been forgotten. The painter and sculptor George Frederic Watts first proposed it in 1887, for Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee, but the scheme wasn't accepted then. In 1898 the vicar of St Botolph's Aldersgate approached him again, hoping it would raise the profile of the park. It was unveiled unfinished in 1900. Ernest George designed the fifty-foot wooden loggia, which shelters a wall with space for 120 ceramic memorial tiles.
